 Arkansas State fires head coach Butch Jones after six seasons
 Daniel Hager @ DanielHagerOn3 47m 0 Share Share 
 Arkansas State has fired head coach Butch Jones , On3’s Pete Nakos reports. The program parts ways with Jones with two regular season games remaining. The Red Wolves sit at 4-6 (2-4) on the season.
 Jones had served as Arkansas State ‘s head coach since the 2021 season. Under Jones’ leadership, the Red Wolves had posted a 30-43 (18-28) record over the past six seasons. They had appeared in three consecutive bowl games prior to this season. That includes wins in the 2024 68 Ventures Bowl and the 2025 Xbox Bowl.
 $39.99 gets you a FULL year of On3 | Rivals national coverage 
 Prior to his stint at Arkansas State , Jones coached at Tennessee (2013-2017), Cincinnati (2010-2012), and Central Michigan (2007-2009). The 58-year-old boasts a 114-97 career record, and was named the Big East Coach of the Year in 2011.
 Jones becomes the seventh FBS coach fired during this cycle. He joins UTEP ‘s Scotty Walden , Florida State ‘s Mike Norvell , Sam Houston ‘s Phil Longo , Baylor ‘s Dave Aranda , NC State ‘s Dave Doeren , and Maryland ‘s Mike Locksley .
 Arkansas State alternated wins and losses over its first four games this season, before losing back-to-back games and then winning back-to-back games. This put the Red Wolves at 4-4 on the season, heading into their final four games. The program, however, has lost its past two games ( UL Monroe and Coastal Carolina ), putting them at 4-6 on the year.
 Butch Jones boasts 114-97 career record across four programs
 Prior to taking over at Arkansas State in 2021, Jones served as an offensive assistant at Alabama from 2018-2020. There’s no doubt Jones would be a valuable asset to a coaching staff, if he decides to returns to an assistant role.
 The Saugatuck, MI native’s most viral moment came following his ‘Champions of Life’ comment, which he made during his tenure as the Tennessee head coach. “They’ve won the biggest championship — that’s the championship of life,” Jones said following a Volunteers loss.
 “The other thing [that took on a life of its own] was ‘Champions of Life’, and that was actually the Big 12 slogan for their conference at that particular time,” Jones said during a conversation with On3’s Andy & Ari this offseason .
 “I was doing it to protect our players. We were heading into Senior Day, and the Josh Dobbs of the world and all of those individuals that had really helped lay the foundation for future success, and the success that we had, and it was just a way of saying that I respect them and respect them for what they did. And they were great people… there’s a lot to take away from that Tennessee experience, and it’ll always be a part of who I am.”
 Jones will now move forward towards his next opportunity elsewhere. Arkansas State will close out the season against Louisiana Tech and Troy .
